_: SEATS ALREADY TAKEN. An earned title is a 1/1: the first claimant takes it and it CLOSES. This file is the only record of which seats are gone, and the STUDIO is its only writer — it is updated in a commit at the moment a kind-2 voucher is signed, which is the same act, so the two cannot drift. A client can never write here, and that is the point: if a browser could close a title, anyone could lock everyone else out of all eleven cards in an afternoon.
_why_not_an_api: There is no endpoint because there is nothing for a player to send. The claim is verified by a person off-site (docs/HERO-UNLOCKS.md §1/§3), so the only write that ever happens is the studio's, and a committed file is a write the studio already knows how to make. It also cannot be down.
_shape: taken[<title id>] = how many of that title's seats are gone. Seats open = title.seats - taken. Anything absent is zero.
_stale_is_the_failure_mode: A seat signed and not recorded here lets a second player clear a closed title and be told it is open. Update this IN THE SAME COMMIT as signing, never after.

notes.twomillion: TWO MILLION FEET — the artist's run, 0x432D71bA14D2602B566dD9e3e098E24859d166c9. One seat, closed. A later 7,000,000 run does not re-open it; that is what ABOVE THE WEATHER exists for.
notes.onemag: ONE MAG — the artist's round, same wallet. One seat, closed.
notes.abovetheweather: ABOVE THE WEATHER — the 7,000,000 RIP ROCKETER run. The SEAT IS RECORDED AS GONE BEFORE THE WINNER'S ADDRESS IS KNOWN, deliberately: what closes a title is that somebody did it, and leaving it open until the paperwork catches up is exactly how a second player gets told they can still have it. The voucher goes into data/hero-vouchers.json when the address arrives.

_seat_before_voucher: A seat is recorded here the moment a run is verified, NOT when its voucher is signed. Those are minutes or days apart, and every minute in between is a window where the site would offer a card that is already spoken for.
